key_insight: PlenopticDreamer synchronizes generative hallucinations across camera views and time, producing spatio-temporally consistent multi-view video re-renderings where prior single-view methods produced inconsistent or flickering hallucinated regions.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of maintaining multi-view spatio-temporal coherence in camera-controlled generative video re-rendering — specifically, preventing inconsistent hallucinations across different viewpoints and over time caused by generative model stochasticity.
method: Introduce a plenoptic-aligned generative framework (PlenopticDreamer) that coordinates hallucinations across views and frames to form a consistent latent/plenoptic field.
Condition generation on camera poses and share synchronized latent signals or cross-view cues so the same scene parts are hallucinated coherently from multiple viewpoints.
Optimize with multi-view and temporal consistency objectives (camera-aware conditioning + consistency losses) to reduce stochastic divergence in rendered regions.
impact: Improves realism and reliability of camera-controlled video re-rendering for applications like virtual cinematography, AR/VR, and multi-view editing by reducing view-inconsistency and temporal flicker in hallucinated content.
visual_elements: Side-by-side multi-view frames: left = prior method (inconsistent hallucinations), right = PlenopticDreamer (consistent across views)
Pipeline diagram: camera poses -> synchronized latent/plenoptic field -> renderer, with consistency loss blocks annotated
Temporal consistency visualization: frame-wise variance or optical-flow based heatmap showing reduced flicker
Bar/line chart comparing multi-view consistency metrics (e.g., multi-view LPIPS, temporal warping error) for baseline vs. PlenopticDreamer
